title: ShardMeter: Sharded and Geo-Distributed Training Without the Guesswork
abstract: arXiv:2608.23840v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training large-scale AI models often outgrows a single data center, demanding sharded, multi-cluster, and decentralized training. However, the huge space of resource allocations makes exhaustive benchmarking and manual tuning impractical, while performance depends on tightly coupled factors like model size, GPU memory, batch size, bandwidth, and sharding strategy. We introduce ShardMeter, a lightweight analytical performance model that predicts the end-to-end runtime of transformer-based workloads across arbitrary sharded, distributed, and even decentralized training. Given a model's characteristics and a target hardware topology, ShardMeter estimates per-GPU and per-island throughput, training cost, total wall-clock time, and identifies performance bottlenecks. translated_title: ShardMeter：无需猜测的分片与地理分布式训练
translated_abstract: 训练大规模AI模型常常超出单一数据中心的能力，需要分片、多集群和去中心化的训练方式。然而，资源分配的庞大空间使得穷举式基准测试和手动调优不切实际，同时性能依赖于紧密耦合的因素，如模型大小、GPU内存、批处理大小、带宽和分片策略。我们引入了ShardMeter，一个轻量级的分析性能模型，能够预测基于Transformer的工作负载在任意分片、分布式甚至去中心化训练中的端到端运行时间。给定模型特征和目标硬件拓扑，ShardMeter可估算每GPU和每岛屿的吞吐量、训练成本、总墙钟时间，并识别性能瓶颈。我们的分析揭示了随着岛屿大小增加而出现的收益递减区间，量化了计算受限与通信受限扩展之间的转换，并评估了超参数权衡。
tldr: ShardMeter提出了一种轻量级分析模型，无需猜测即可预测分片和地理分布式训练的性能瓶颈与运行时间，帮助优化资源分配。
en_tdlr: ShardMeter introduces a lightweight analytical model that predicts performance bottlenecks and runtime for sharded and geo-distributed training without guesswork, aiding resource allocation optimization.
